sentences.text: Genghis Khan -LRB- -LSB- ˈdʒɛŋɡɪs_ˈkɑːn -RSB- , usually pronounced -LSB- ˈɡɛŋɡɪs_ˈkɑːn -RSB- Чингис хаан , Çingis hán -LSB- t͡ʃʰiŋɡɪs xaːŋ -RSB- , c. 1162 August 18 , 1227 -RRB- , born Temüjin , was the Great Khan and founder of the Mongol Empire , which became the largest contiguous empire in history after his death .	Mongol Empire	Mongol Empire	Khan	Khan (title)	Great Khan	Khagan	Mongol	Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet	largest contiguous empire	World's largest empires
He came to power by uniting many of the nomadic tribes of Northeast Asia .	Northeast Asia	Northeast Asia

After founding the Empire and being proclaimed `` Genghis Khan '' , he started the Mongol invasions that conquered most of Eurasia .	Khan	Khan (title)	Mongol	Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet	Mongol invasions	Mongol invasions	conquered	Mongol invasions and conquests	Eurasia	Eurasia

Campaigns initiated in his lifetime include those against the Qara Khitai , Caucasus , and Khwarazmian , Western Xia and Jin dynasties .	Qara Khitai	Mongol conquest of the Qara Khitai	Caucasus	Caucasus	Khwarazmian	Mongol invasion of Khwarezmia	Western Xia	Mongol conquest of Western Xia	Jin	Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty

These campaigns were often accompanied by large-scale massacres of the civilian populations -- especially in the Khwarazmian and Western Xia controlled lands .	Khwarazmian	Mongol invasion of Khwarezmia	Western Xia	Mongol conquest of Western Xia

By the end of his life , the Mongol Empire occupied a substantial portion of Central Asia and China .	Mongol Empire	Mongol Empire	Mongol	Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet	Central Asia	Central Asia	China	Song dynasty
Before Genghis Khan died he assigned Ögedei Khan as his successor .	Khan	Khan (title)	Ögedei Khan	Ögedei Khan	Ögedei	Ögedei Khan
Later his grandsons split his empire into khanates .	split his empire	Division of the Mongol Empire
He died in 1227 after defeating the Western Xia .	Western Xia	Mongol conquest of Western Xia
He was buried in an unmarked grave somewhere in Mongolia .	Mongolia	Mongolia	unmarked grave	Tomb of Genghis Khan

His descendants extended the Mongol Empire across most of Eurasia by conquering or creating vassal states in all of modern-day China , Korea , the Caucasus , Central Asia , and substantial portions of Eastern Europe and Southwest Asia .	Mongol Empire	Mongol Empire	Mongol	Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet	Eurasia	Eurasia	Caucasus	Caucasus	Central Asia	Central Asia	China	Song dynasty	vassal	vassal	Korea	Korea	Southwest Asia	Southwest Asia	Europe	Europe
Many of these invasions repeated the earlier large-scale slaughters of local populations .
As a result , Genghis Khan and his empire have a fearsome reputation in local histories .	Khan	Khan (title)
Beyond his military accomplishments , Genghis Khan also advanced the Mongol Empire in other ways .	Mongol Empire	Mongol Empire	Khan	Khan (title)	Mongol	Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet
He decreed the adoption of the Uyghur script as the Mongol Empire 's writing system .	Mongol Empire	Mongol Empire	Mongol	Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet	Uyghur script	Old Uyghur alphabet

He also practiced meritocracy and encouraged religious tolerance in the Mongol Empire , and unified the nomadic tribes of Northeast Asia .	Mongol Empire	Mongol Empire	Mongol	Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet	Northeast Asia	Northeast Asia	meritocracy	meritocracy	religious tolerance	religious tolerance
Present-day Mongolians regard him as the founding father of Mongolia .	Mongolia	Mongolia	Mongolians	Mongols

Although known for the brutality of his campaigns and considered by many to have been a genocidal ruler , Genghis Khan is also credited with bringing the Silk Road under one cohesive political environment .	Khan	Khan (title)	genocidal	Genocide	Silk Road	Silk Road

This brought communication and trade from Northeast Asia into Muslim Southwest Asia and Christian Europe , thus expanding the horizons of all three cultural areas .	Northeast Asia	Northeast Asia	Southwest Asia	Southwest Asia	Muslim	Muslim	Europe	Europe
